experiment: Confirmation of the remaining-Prefill blocking formula with a 5% TTFT profile-uncertainty reserve

selection_record.result: On 528 cached physical conditions, remaining-Prefill blocking reduced false rejections from 16 to 11 with false acceptances staying at 0. TTFT reserves of 0%, 2.5%, and 5% were tied on these verdict counts; 10% added false rejections.
selection_record.rationale: Use the physically motivated remaining-service blocking rule. Among tied low-cost TTFT reserves, 5% matches the smallest profile-error stress magnitude already used for uncertainty analysis and provides a one-sided safety allowance before confirmation. The choice is frozen before evaluating the long workloads.
selection_record.not_claimed: The 5% value is not fitted as an optimum and is not yet a final production margin.

guardrails.arrival_model: same AICCC/HELIX Azure-derived arrivals and intensity time-scaling
guardrails.latency_metrics: standard first-output TTFT and request-average post-first TPOT
guardrails.network: unchanged residual-time to per-link bandwidth commitment equations

success_questions: Does the candidate avoid increasing false acceptance on the long workloads?
Does it reduce false rejection relative to the current accounting?
Does it move the sampled maximum-safe-load edge closer to the HELIX reference?
Does every accounting-only comparison preserve the same J0 trajectory?
